items.title: SpaceX launches first Starship V3 but loses booster over Gulf of Mexico

featured_image.name: SpaceX's upgraded Starship V3 blasts off in debut test flight from Texas |  Reuters

items.description:
SpaceX launched its upgraded Starship V3 megarocket on Friday evening from Starbase, Texas, marking the debut of the company's most powerful rocket design yet. While the upper stage successfully deployed 22 dummy Starlink satellites and completed a controlled splashdown in the Indian Ocean, the Super Heavy booster crashed uncontrolled into the Gulf of Mexico after its engines failed to perform as planned.

The flight, which lifted off at 5:33 p.m. CDT from SpaceX's new Pad 2, came one day after a hydraulic pin on the launch tower arm failed to retract, scrubbing the first attempt at T-minus 40 seconds. Upper-level winds pushed the launch from its initial 5:30 p.m. window to 6:30 p.m. CDT on Friday.[1][2]

items.title: 4 dead, 90 trapped in China coal mine after CO buildup

featured_image.name: Chinese coal miners killed by carbon monoxide poisoning

items.description: Four workers have been confirmed dead and 90 remain trapped underground after carbon monoxide levels exceeded safe limits at a coal mine in Changzhi City, in northern China's Shanxi Province, according to a Reuters report citing the state news agency Xinhua.[1][2]

items.title: Iran condemns US sanctions on its envoy to Lebanon

items.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry on Friday strongly condemned the US Treasury Department's decision to sanction Tehran's designated ambassador to Lebanon, Mohammad Reza Sheibani, calling the move "illegal and unjustified" and accusing Washington of violating international law and the UN Charter.[1][2][3]

items.title: WHO upgrades Congo Ebola risk to 'very high' as cases surge
items.description:
The World Health Organization on Friday upgraded its risk assessment for the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo from "high" to "very high" at the national level, as the rapidly escalating epidemic now encompasses nearly 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.[1]

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the outbreak is "spreading rapidly" and warned that the actual scale is likely far larger than official figures suggest. There are now 82 confirmed cases in the DRC along with seven confirmed fatalities, but Tedros indicated the true toll could exceed 1,000 infections, with cases significantly underreported for months before detection.[2][1]

items.title: Rubio cites 'slight progress' in US-Iran peace talks

featured_image.name: Marco Rubio says U.S. expects Iran response on peace deal 'today'

items.description:
Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi in Tehran as Islamabad pushed to narrow the remaining gaps between Washington and Tehran in stalled peace negotiations. Speaking at a NATO foreign ministers' meeting in Helsingborg, Sweden, Secretary of State Marco Rubio offered a cautious assessment of the diplomatic efforts.

"There has been some slight progress. I don't want to exaggerate it, but there's been a little bit of movement, and that's good," Rubio told reporters on Friday.[1][2][3]

items.title: Palestinian envoy drops UN vice presidency bid after US threats

items.description: Palestinian Ambassador Riyad Mansour has withdrawn his candidacy for a vice president position at the UN General Assembly following pressure from the Trump administration, the United Nations confirmed on Thursday. Lebanon's ambassador will assume the role in his place.[1][2]

items.title: Russia developing seabed nuclear missiles, German investigation finds

featured_image.name: Russia slates drills for nuclear forces

items.description:
NATO intelligence services have been closely tracking Russia's Northern Fleet amid growing concerns that Moscow is advancing a secret program to deploy nuclear-armed missiles on the Arctic Ocean seabed, according to an investigation published on May 21 by German public broadcasters WDR and NDR. The report identifies a classified project codenamed "Skif," under which Russia is believed to be developing remote-controlled missile systems housed in sealed containers dropped from submarines to the ocean floor.[1][2][3]

The revelation comes as Russia wraps up its largest nuclear exercises in years, a three-day drill running from May 19 through May 21 that mobilized nearly 65,000 troops, over 200 missile launchers, 140 aircraft, 73 surface vessels, and 13 submarines — including eight strategic nuclear submarines.[4][5]

items.title: Trump, Rubio reject Iran's plan for Hormuz toll system

items.description: Iran is in active talks with Oman to establish a permanent toll system for ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, formalizing Tehran's control over one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints. The move drew sharp rebukes from both President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Thursday.
